approach: Add one pure reading check, `check_behavior_test_design`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs, wired as one `step!` line directly after `check_code_survey`. It reads only the reading's `Code survey:` assumptions, criteria and deliverables. It parses the survey into labelled clauses (`Entry point:`, `Gate order:`, `Stop gate:`, `Reuses:`, `Output:`, `Direct check:`) and judges each clause alone. (a) The entry-point and gate-order clauses hold identifiers, and the stop gate equals one of the gate-order identifiers. (b) The `Reuses:` clause names an identifier or says "no existing function". (c) The `Output:` clause says "no new output", names record evidence through the existing `names_record_evidence`, or holds a schema tag. A typed record named only by a round-trip identifier also needs a behavior criterion that names it and a deliverable that can hold the test. (d) Each behavior criterion is covered by its own `Direct check:` clause with a measurement verb, and no skip switch or internal-helper read is the means of measurement. Round 3 changes: (1) The reader guide `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE` is rewritten in place to teach the labelled format with a filled-in example, so the reader can comply on its first attempt. The error template is that same example, extracted at run time, so the guide, the error and the tests have one source. (2) A backtick-quoted token is an identifier, so single-word names such as `replay` count. (3) Only a negator in the same comma, semicolon or full-stop segment cancels a skip-switch or helper phrase, and refusal words do not cancel. (4) A typed-record round-trip needs a deliverable that can hold the test, not just any crates/ file. (5) One `Direct check:` clause may cite at most two criteria. The check cannot read the repository, because the reading gate runs without one (replay.rs:50-55), so "contradicts the code" means contradicting a rule this check enforces or the reading itself. The doc comment says so. The declared share is the reading's criterion 4, 'expected 20% of newly refused readings'. The check is not weakened to meet it.

decisions.choice: Judge the survey by labelled clauses, not by whole-text phrase search. A clause runs from its label (case-insensitive, at the start of the text or after whitespace or a full stop) to the next label. A repeated label, or a label in a second `Code survey:` assumption, adds to the same clause. Position finding uses ASCII lowercase on whitespace-normalised original text, so identifier case (`AnyRecord`) is kept.
decisions.reason: Each part is read inside its own clause, so a word such as 'directly' or 'calls' in a description of the code cannot stand for a measurement, and the stop gate is looked up only in the `Gate order:` clause. The reading is a plain `Vec<String>` of assumptions (surveys.rs:117-124), so labels are the only structure available without changing the Reading type.

decisions.choice: (a): `Entry point:` holds an identifier. `Gate order:` holds at least two distinct identifiers. `Stop gate:` holds an identifier equal, after trimming backticks and `()`, to one in the gate order. An identifier is a backtick-quoted token with no whitespace, or a bare whitespace token (trailing punctuation trimmed) that contains `_` or `::` or ends in `()`. A stop gate in prose has no identifier and is refused as missing (a); a stop gate not in the order is refused as a contradiction.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2: single-word gate functions such as `replay` (replay.rs:365) count when backticked, and the template's names are backticked. Bare prose words are still not identifiers, so 'the resolution step' names no gate.

decisions.choice: (b): `Reuses:` holds an identifier, or the phrase 'no existing function', or both. Refuse an absent or empty clause, or one with neither. Partial reuse ('reuses `names_record_evidence`; no existing function checks gate order') is accepted.

decisions.choice: (c): the `Output:` clause passes when `names_record_evidence(clause)` holds (it already matches `AnyRecord`, `check_record_file` and round-trip identifiers, surveys.rs:164-175), or a new `names_schema_tag` finds a token that starts `athena.` with `/` then digits, or it says 'no new output' or 'no new record' and no deliverable is a record or data deliverable. Contradiction: the clause says 'no new output' with no record evidence while a deliverable satisfies `is_record_or_data_deliverable`. A typed record named only by a round-trip identifier needs two more things. First, a behavior criterion that names a round-trip token (the shared predicate `is_round_trip_token`, extracted from `names_record_evidence` with no behaviour change). Second, a deliverable that can hold the test: its path has a `tests/` directory, or ends `records.rs`, or appears in the Output clause. A kind (`AnyRecord`, `check_record_file`) or schema tag needs no round-trip deliverable, as the request allows 'a record kind the records check already accepts'.

decisions.choice: (d): each `Direct check:` clause must hold a measurement verb (`count`, `counts`, `counting`, `counted`, `asserts`, `asserting`, `compares`, `observes`). Every behavior criterion number must be cited by a clause (`criterion 2`, `criteria 2 and 3`, `criteria 2-3`). A clause with no number covers all behavior criteria only when the reading has exactly one. One clause may cite at most two criteria; a clause that cites more, including a range such as `criteria 1-7`, is refused with 'one direct check covers N criteria; write one clause per criterion or per pair'. Uncovered criterion numbers are listed in the error.
decisions.reason: The request asks for a direct check for each claimed property. Answers finding 5: a generic verb over a wide range no longer covers everything. A clause can still state a measurement that is untrue; that limit goes in the doc comment, and the plan critic and verifier judge it.

decisions.choice: Skip-switch and internal-helper contradictions, scoped to the means of measurement. Phrases: `skip switch`, `skip flag`, `test-only switch`, `--skip`, `internal helper`, `private helper`. Split the text into segments at commas, semicolons, full stops and the word `but`. In a `Direct check:` clause an occurrence counts unless a negator (`no`, `not`, `never`, `without`, `nor`, `instead of`) stands earlier in the SAME segment. Refusal words (`refuse`, `refused`, `reject`) do not cancel; only a refusal verb right before the phrase (within two words, as in 'refuses a skip switch') cancels. In a behavior criterion an occurrence counts only when a measuring-means phrase is within 4 words before it in the same segment and no negator precedes it in that segment. The means phrases are `through`, `via`, `using`, `by reading`, `by inspecting`, and `measured/checked/verified/tested` followed by `by` or `with`. A bare `read` is not a means phrase.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3 and keeps the earlier fix. A single early `not` or `refused` no longer disables the check for the whole clause, so 'Direct check: criterion 2 asserts the reading is refused, measured through a skip switch' is refused. The request's wording ('counting planner, producer or model calls, not reads of an internal helper and not a skip switch added just for the test'), the template, and this job's own criterion 3 ('a property check that is a skip switch or a read of an internal helper' has no means phrase) are all accepted. Limit: a criterion that describes a refusal fixture with 'through a skip switch' is refused and must be reworded; the doc comment states it.

rejected.option: A negator or refusal word anywhere earlier in the clause cancels

demonstrations.method: Grep for the function, its reuse of the named helpers, the error text and the step line; a unit test reads `refusing_check`'s source for the step order.
demonstrations.command: Grep -n "pub fn check_behavior_test_design|changes_code_with_behavior_criterion\(|names_record_evidence\(|step!\(check_code_survey|step!\(check_behavior_test_design" crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs && cargo test -p athena-core design_check_has_one_step_line
demonstrations.observes: surveys.rs has `pub fn check_behavior_test_design(reading: &Reading) -> Result<()>`. Its first statement calls `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`, and it calls `names_record_evidence` on the `Output:` clause. Its `bail!` starts 'the reading was refused because', names each missing part as (a), (b), (c) or (d), and prints the guide's example as the template. checks.rs has `step!(check_behavior_test_design(reading));` on the line right after `step!(check_code_survey(reading));`, and the test asserts that order.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no function and no step line the grep finds neither, and `design_check_has_one_step_line_after_the_survey_step` fails.
demonstrations.seam: Static grep plus a unit test over the source text of `refusing_check`, the same technique as `history_fixture_has_one_step_line` (reading.rs ~8206, exists). Step 4 adds the new test.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests and corpus cases run the real gate on four otherwise complete code readings, each omitting one part, and on complete readings. The tests are written by the plan's steps and not yet run.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core design_check && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.observes: `design_check_refuses_each_omitted_part` builds four readings from `code_reading` and the complete survey, lacking in turn (a) the gate order and stop gate, (b) the `Reuses:` clause, (c) the `Output:` kind (and the round-trip identifier), (d) the `Direct check:` clause. Each asserts `refusing_check` returns `check_behavior_test_design` and that the error names only the omitted letter. More refused fixtures: a stop gate in prose (a); 'directly' and 'calls' only in a description of the code outside a `Direct check:` clause (d); two behavior criteria with one cited (d, names the uncovered number); one clause citing `criteria 1-4` (d). Accepted: `design_check_accepts_a_complete_reading`, parts spread over two `Code survey:` assumptions, labels in other case with extra spaces, partial reuse, identifiers as `f()`, `a::b` and single-word backticked `replay`, and the guide's example (`design_check_accepts_the_guide_example`). Corpus refusing ids: `design-missing-gate-order-and-stop-gate`, `design-missing-reused-function`, `design-missing-record-kind-or-roundtrip`, `design-missing-direct-check`, `design-stop-gate-in-prose`, `design-direct-check-words-only-in-code-description`, `design-one-clause-covers-many-criteria`. Corpus accepting ids: `design-complete-reading-accepted`, `design-partial-reuse-accepted`, `design-split-across-surveys-accepted`, `design-single-word-backtick-identifiers-accepted`, `design-guide-example-accepted`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, `check_code_survey` accepts all four incomplete readings because it needs only a crates/ path (surveys.rs:203-216), so the refuser assertions fail. `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` fails if the step exists with no refusing case.
demonstrations.seam: Production entries `check_behavior_test_design`, `refusing_check` and `check_reading_acceptance` (checks.rs:492-551, exist). Fixtures are plain `Reading` values built with `code_reading` and `SURVEY` (reading.rs ~7037-7060, exist; step 4 makes `SURVEY` the complete survey) and the corpus `base_reading` and `case` helpers (refusal_corpus.rs ~172, 241, exist). Step 1 adds `survey_example` and the clause parser. There is no double: the check is a pure function and no model is called.

demonstrations.method: Fixtures each change one field of a complete reading to contradict a rule, plus negated, verbatim and refusal-word twins.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core design_check_contradiction && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.observes: Refused with `check_behavior_test_design`: a stop gate not in the `Gate order:` clause; a record or data deliverable (`crates/athena-data/src/records.rs`, or a created `crates/.../records/x.json`) beside 'Output: no new output'; a typed record with no round-trip identifier and no schema tag; a typed record whose round-trip identifier no behavior criterion names; a typed record with a round-trip identifier and criterion but no deliverable under tests/, no records.rs and no path in the Output clause; a `Direct check:` that measures 'through a skip switch'; 'Direct check: criterion 2 asserts the reading is refused, measured through a skip switch' (refusal word does not cancel); a criterion that checks 'by reading an internal helper'. Accepted twins: 'counts planner calls on the fake, not a skip switch or a read of an internal helper'; the request's exact wording 'counting planner, producer or model calls, not reads of an internal helper and not a skip switch added just for the test'; this job's own criterion 3 text; the guide's example. Corpus refusing ids: `design-stop-gate-not-in-order`, `design-new-typed-record-without-roundtrip-deliverable`, `design-typed-record-roundtrip-without-test-file`, `design-record-deliverable-beside-no-new-output`, `design-criterion-uses-skip-switch`, `design-criterion-reads-internal-helper`, `design-refusal-word-does-not-cancel-skip-switch`. Accepting ids: `design-negated-skip-switch-accepted`, `design-request-wording-accepted`, `design-template-verbatim-accepted` (the guide's example).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the contradiction rules every label is present and the readings pass, so the refusal assertions fail. A version that refuses on any mention, uses a 3-word window or lets a refusal word cancel fails the accepted twins or the refusal-word fixture.
demonstrations.seam: Same production entries and fixtures as criterion 2. Step 1 adds the segment splitter, the negator logic and `names_schema_tag`; each test calls the production function on a reading with one field changed. Exists after step 1.

demonstrations.method: Two parts. (1) A fixture replay through the production `replay` function proves the declared-share arithmetic and that the rule is newly refusing. (2) Athena's own replay at verification runs on real records. Part (1) does not measure the real share.
demonstrations.observes: (1) `design_check_replay_share_is_within_the_declared_range` builds 10 `ReplayCase` values: 2 code readings with the old short survey (newly refused), 4 with the complete survey, 4 docs readings. Every case passes all later checks. For each newly refused case it asserts the reading with the complete survey is accepted by `check_reading_text`. The base checker is `check_reading_text` on that swapped reading; the candidate is `check_reading_text` on the reading as it is. The declaration comes from `replay_declaration_of` on a reading whose criterion reads 'expected 20% of newly refused readings'. It asserts `!run.held`, at least 1 newly refused, and `newly_refused * 100 <= total * replay_limit_percent(Some(20))`. A second run with a candidate that refuses every code reading asserts `run.held`. (2) At verification the host runs `replay_cases` over the newest 50 accepted readings (replay.rs:9, 140-156; run/mod.rs ~2246-2402) and records the Replay and its `held` flag. State needed: the host's `records/` with accepted readings. The plan neither runs nor waits for it; the verifier reads the recorded Replay. The real share is unmeasured and likely above 20%, so an independent expectation does not yet exist; see open_questions.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check newly refused more than 25% of the fixtures, `run.held` is true and the assertion fails. If it refused nothing, the 'at least 1' assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entries `replay`, `replay_declaration_of`, `replay_limit_percent` and `check_reading_text` (replay.rs:54, 289-308, 365; exist). `ReplayCase` values and checker closures are built with the existing `replay_case` helper and `base_checker` pattern (reading.rs ~6466-6545, exist); step 7 adds the test. The closures only call `check_reading_text`; the logic under test is the production check.

open_questions: User: The accepted reading fixes 'expected 20% of newly refused readings' (limit 25% with the 5-point margin). Most accepted code readings in the newest 50 probably carry only a short `Code survey:` with none of the labelled parts, so the real newly refused share is probably well above 25% and the host replay would hold this job at verification. Code cannot show the real share, because records/ is not in the snapshot. Do you want the reading revised to declare a higher share with a reason sentence (a criterion with 'because' and 'refuse(d)' or 'past readings', which `replay_declaration` accepts above 25%), or accept that the job may be held?
